name: isort-fad14135-blind26-ots
instr:
# isort-regen

A tool that tidies the block of declarations at the top of a Python file — the ones that pull in other modules — now gets that job wrong in a number of ways, and in a couple of cases refuses work it used to do. Nothing about the language changed and nothing about the callers changed. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been noticed from the outside, written as the actions people took and the answers they got back.

Putting names in order has become sensitive to capitalisation in two independent ways. A file naming one lower-case thing alongside two capitalised ones, run with one declaration per row and alphabetical ordering inside a group, comes back with the capitalised ones pulled ahead though nobody asked for case to matter; the same reshuffling appears when the code arrives on standard input, and a single declaration naming two things no longer puts the lower-case one first. Separately, when whole-module and from-a-module declarations are made to rank together inside one group, a capitalised module is no longer kept beside its lower-case twin, so a file already arranged that way comes back rearranged. Runs that explicitly ask for case to matter still return their input untouched.
